successors.note: 'subdued in the early 20th century by the Dutch colonial government' (page); the year 1905 is the researcher's bridging from the South Sulawesi campaign page's title; the header runs the state 'c. 1400-1957' and the page has it transformed into the Wajo Regency.

capitals.name: Tosora
capitals.note: The text names Tosora as the 'walled capital city'; the earliest seat was Cinnotabiq, which was 'transformed into Wajoq in the early 15th century'. Coordinates approximate.

correction.text: Wajo round the walled capital Tosora and the central lakes (the Wajo Regency of today)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no row). The page names Tosora and 'the central lakes' and the Cenrana River, no area or frontier; the disc is the researcher's stand-in for the Wajo Regency. The page does not mention Lake Tempe, Sengkang or Pammana.

ledger.note: c. 1400: Cinnotabiq becomes Wajoq. 'It was founded in the 15th century, and reached its peak in the 18th century'; Cinnotabiq was 'transformed into Wajoq in the early 15th century' under La Tenribali; header 'c. 1400-1957'.

region.text: Wajo round the walled capital Tosora and the central lakes (the Wajo Regency of today)

ledger.note: 1610: Gowa forces Wajo to Islam. Gowa's campaigns are described as 'forcing Soppeng to embrace Islam in 1609, Wajoq in 1610, and Bone in 1611'. The page gives the year of the conversion, not a campaign or its ground; the ledger has Wajo holding its land.

region.text: Wajo round the walled capital Tosora and the central lakes (the Wajo Regency of today)

ledger.note: 1610: closed in the year it opens. The page records the forced conversion and nothing about a Gowa garrison; the sultanate-of-gowa dossier has no Wajo event.

region.text: Wajo round the walled capital Tosora and the central lakes (the Wajo Regency of today)

ledger.note: 1905: the Dutch take Wajo (bridging). The page says Wajo was 'subdued in the early 20th century by the Dutch colonial government' and links the South Sulawesi expeditions of 1905; it gives no year for Wajo itself.

region.text: Wajo round the walled capital Tosora and the central lakes (the Wajo Regency of today)

ledger.note: 1905: Wajo ends as a sovereign state (bridging, page silent). The page has it 'continued to exist in some form up to the mid-20th century' and become the Wajo Regency.

zones.text: Wajo round the walled capital Tosora and the central lakes (the Wajo Regency of today)

wars.outcome: Gowa forced 'Soppeng to embrace Islam in 1609, Wajoq in 1610, and Bone in 1611'.
wars.note: No ground changed hands on the page.

wars.name: Makassar War (Wajo's part)
wars.outcome: Wajo 'still refused to abide by the Treaty of Bungaya' (page, no date); the Makassar War page does not mention Wajo.
wars.note: The Treaty of Timurung of 1582 was 'a mutual defense pact initiated by Bone'; La Maddukelleng was arung matoa 1736-1754 and led Peneki.

certainty.note: The page gives no frontier; Wajo's lands round the lakes were a federation of districts.

sources.title: Wajo Kingdom
sources.note: Header c. 1400-1957, Cinnotabiq to Wajoq, Tosora, the 1582 Treaty of Timurung, Gowa's Islamisation 1609-1611, 1736-1754, the early 20th century Dutch.

sources.title: Makassar War
sources.note: Opened to date Wajo's part: it does not mention Wajo, Luwu or Tallo; Bone and Soppeng rose against Gowa in 1666-67, the Treaty of Bungaya was signed 18 November 1667, Somba Opu fell in June 1669, Bone replaced Gowa from 1672.

notes: Cliopatria has no row for Wajo. Wikidata id not looked up (wikidata.org unreachable): null. The pages give no Wajo territory: the disc on Tosora is the researcher's. End 1905 is bridging: the header runs the state to 1957 and the page says Wajo 'continued to exist in some form up to the mid-20th century'. The 1736-1754 arung matoa La Maddukelleng, the 1670 fall of Wajo to Bone and the VOC, and Wajo's peak in the 18th century are not dated by territory on the page. Gazetteer: Tosora is not in places.jsonl. Soppeng and Tallo, the other Bugis polities in the scope list, are not written (Tallo is merged into Gowa in the sultanate-of-gowa dossier).
